messages.content: 請幫我找出下週五在柏林和巴黎附近的所有古典音樂會，我只對有停車位的音樂會感興趣。

function.name: concert_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby concerts based on specific criteria like genre and availability of parking. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city where the user wants to find a concert.

date.description: The date on which the user wants to attend a concert.

genre.description: The genre of music of the concert.

message.reasoning:
The user wants all classical concerts next Friday near Berlin and Paris, only those with parking. We need to call the function twice: one for Berlin, one for Paris. The function requires location, date, genre, amenities optional. We'll set date to next Friday's date. Need to compute next Friday from today (Nov 4, 2026). Let's calculate: Today is Nov 4, 2026. That's a Thursday? Actually let's check: 2026-11-04. I can quickly approximate: 2026-01-01 was a Sunday? But easier: Use known reference: 2025-01-01 was a Wednesday? Wait, maybe we should not rely on memory; but we can approximate: 2026-01-01 is a Monday? Let's do quick calculation: 2020-01-01 was Wednesday. 2021-01-01 was Friday. 2022-01-01 was Saturday. 2023-01-01 was Sunday. 2024-01-01 was Monday. 2025-01-01 was Wednesday. 2026-01-01 will be Thursday? Actually 2025-01-01 was Wednesday, so 2026-01-01 will be Thursday (since 2025 is not leap year). So 2026-01-01 is Thursday. Then 2026-11-04 is 10 months later. 2026-01-01 to 2026-11-04 is 307 days? Let's count: Jan 31 days, Feb 28, Mar 31, Apr 30, May 31, Jun 30, Jul 31, Aug 31, Sep 30, Oct 31, plus 4 days in November. Sum: 31+28=59, +31=90, +30=120, +31=151, +30=181, +31=212, +31=243, +30=273, +31=304, +4=308. So 308 days after Jan 1. 308 mod 7 = 308/7=44 exactly, remainder 0. So same day of week: Thursday. So 2026-11-04 is Thursday. Next Friday is 2026-11-05. So date param: "2026-11-05". We'll call function for Berlin and Paris.

We need to pass amenities: "Parking". The function signature says amenities?: "Parking" | "Food and Beverages" | "VIP Seating" | "Disability Access"[]; default: ["Parking"]. It expects an array? The type shows union of string or array? It's ambiguous. But we can pass ["Parking"].

We'll call function twice.
